lines.text: Checkout bugs cost sales, and they often ship without anyone noticing. This is CheckoutGuard.
Kane CLI tests your checkout, a coding agent fixes what breaks, and Kane checks the fix before anything merges.
In our demo store, three mugs at eighteen dollars should cost fifty-four. The cart says eighteen.
Here's the CheckoutGuard dashboard, with the three checkout journeys we test.
I run the cart journey. Kane CLI drives a real browser, step by step, like a customer.
Kane fails it, and says why: the subtotal stayed at eighteen dollars.
I ask for a fix. Claude Code works in an isolated copy of the store, with no shell, no web, and no access to the tests.
The fix is one line, and the unit checks pass.
Then Kane reruns the same journey. Only a Kane pass marks the repair verified.
I review the diff, and Kane's before and after screenshots.
Then I approve, and it's merged.
Every checkout tested. Every fix verified. That's CheckoutGuard.
